The Florida State Seminoles will travel to Louisville to take on the Cardinals in Week 6 of the 2026 regular season. The game is set for Friday, October 9, 2026, at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium in Louisville, Kentucky, and will be broadcast on ESPN. Florida State enters this contest with a 3-2 overall record, including a 0-1 mark on the road. Florida State is coming off a dominant 38-7 victory over the Virginia Cavaliers, showcasing their ability to control the game on the ground with 282 rushing yards. Despite their strong home performances, the Seminoles have struggled on the road. They will look to secure their first away win of the season against a conference opponent. The Louisville Cardinals, with a 2-3 record, are looking to bounce back after a narrow 31-28 loss to North Carolina State. Louisville has shown strength at home with a 2-1 record, including a high-scoring 41-31 victory over SMU. As they prepare to host Florida State, the Cardinals aim to leverage their home-field advantage to improve their conference standing. Louisville vs Florida State At a Glance (Week 6) Game Date and Time: Friday, October 9, 2026 at 7:00 PM Venue: L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium in Louisville, KY — Outdoor Field TV Channel: ESPN Florida State Record: 3-2 overall, 0-1 on the road Louisville Record: 2-3 overall, 2-1 at home Game Odds: Louisville -180, Florida State +149, Spread - Louisville -4 (-111) Louisville Cardinals Prepare for a Showdown at Home Offensive Performance The Louisville Cardinals have been effective on the offensive end this season, currently ranking 15th nationally with 193 points scored. Their passing game, led by quarterback Lincoln Kienholz, has been particularly strong, accumulating 1,437 yards and ranking 18th. The rushing attack has also contributed significantly, with 1,049 yards placing them 22nd in the nation. Keyjuan Brown and Isaac Brown have been instrumental in the ground game, combining for nearly 700 rushing yards. In the air, Tre Richardson has been the go-to target, amassing 445 receiving yards. The offense's ability to move the chains is evident with 117 first downs, ranking 16th nationally. Defensive Struggles On the defensive side, the Cardinals have faced challenges, allowing 146 points and ranking 97th in the nation. However, they have been impressive in creating turnovers, ranking 5th with 4 interceptions and 6th with 3 fumbles recovered. The defense has also generated pressure, recording 8 sacks to rank 14th. Despite these efforts, the Cardinals will need to tighten their coverage and improve their tackling to reduce the points allowed. Players like Antonio Watts, who is out with a knee injury, will be missed as the team seeks defensive consistency. Recent Form and Injuries Louisville enters this game with a 2-3 record in their last five games, most recently losing to North Carolina State 31-28. Injuries have been a concern, with several key players like Kris Hughes and Antonio Watts unavailable. Additionally, several players are questionable, which could impact depth and performance against strong opposition. Travis Egan and Sam Secrest are among those listed as questionable, potentially affecting both the offensive and defensive units. The Cardinals will need contributions from their depth to overcome these setbacks. Key Players to Watch Lincoln Kienholz remains a pivotal figure for the Cardinals, with over 1,394 passing yards and 9 touchdowns. His connection with Tre Richardson and Lawayne McCoy will be crucial in stretching the field and finding the end zone. On special teams, Carson Hilbert has been reliable, converting 6 field goals and 20 extra points this season. His accuracy could be a difference-maker in tight games. away.blurb: Florida State linebacker Noah LaVallee was downgraded from probable to out after there was previously hope he would play in Week 5. Noah's brother and fellow linebacker, Caleb, is currently listed as probable for the upcoming game. Florida State's linebacker depth just took another hit with Noah LaVallee downgraded to out for Week 5 Florida State entered the game with a handful of players already confirmed to be out of the Week 5 game, but losing LaVallee particularly stings since he is a player filling in due to the injuries. LaVallee did not record any stats through the first three games, but began to work into the rotation against Central Arkansas with 21 snaps. The injury list is still rather long, even with a handful of players removed. Defensive back Quindarrius Jones and Caleb LaVallee are still listed as probable for the upcoming game against Virginia. Florida State and Virginia both released lengthy injury reports ahead of the Week 5 battle on Saturday. Both teams will be without a good chunk of the roster, but the key difference is that the Seminoles will be without multiple players at a vital position, and another player from the same position just joined that list. 2026 has not been the most productive season up to this point for Florida State, with a handful of players powering through bumps and bruises to compensate for the number of more serious injuries, particularly on defense. Starting safety Ashlynd Barker has been playing through a broken bone in his arm, although somewhat controversially , to make up for the shocking injury total. Without Noah and potentially Caleb in the picture, the slack will need to be picked up by the likes of Karon Maycock and AJ Cottrill. Maycock, a freshman, saw his first real action of the season against Central Arkansas and recorded three total tackles. Cottrill, on the other hand, saw action against SMU and Central Arkansas, totaling two tackles. During the Week 3 game against Alabama in Tuscaloosa, Florida State only played four linebackers and opted to use plenty of defensive backs. With Mikai Gbayor, Chris Jones, and Omar Graham Jr. all expected to play in Week 5, the Seminoles' staff might just give the remaining snaps at linebacker to the more experienced Cottrill. The only issue, however, is that Alabama and Virginia are far different teams in terms of how the offense attacks opposing defenses. Virginia is going to look to keep the football on the ground for most of the game. When combined with the play-action heavy passing attack, the Seminoles' linebackers could tire easily, which will force more of the remaining depth into the game. The updated injury report delivered a few positive bits of news for Florida State, as Ashlynd Barker, Chris Jones, KJ Kirkland, Donny Hiebert, and Xavier Tiller were all upgraded

away.headline: Virginia's lengthy injury report gives Florida State an obvious Week 5 game plan
away.blurb: The Seminoles essentially have to win this weekend versus the Virginia Cavaliers to get their season back on track. Mike Norvell is coaching for his job, and the only real way to do that is by essentially winning out in ACC play. This is an extremely daunting task, but the only way to eat an elephant is by taking it one bite at a time, and that is exactly what the game will be. Now that the injury reports have gone up for the matchup , it is easier to determine how this game will look. While both teams have a number of key players out, the focus for Florida State fans should be on the losses for Virginia on their defensive line. The biggest name to look for in that area is defensive tackle Jason Hammond. Hammond entered the season as one of the players with the most hype on the Virginia defensive front. This was supposed to be the year when Hammond finally took those next steps and solidified himself as one of the better linemen in the conference, but now it appears his return this season is in question. Kromah appears poised to remain the bell cow and should mostly see the opposing starters, but Wisner is where the lack of depth for Virginia will start to show itself. As the Cavaliers start to sub players out, FSU will try to spell Kromah with the equally-capable Wisner, and that is where FSU will need to force their will on a depleted opponent. The Wisner hype was perhaps a little too premature coming into the season based on his limited reps leading up to last week, but he has an easy path towards showing why the Seminoles put so much faith in him with a nice chunk of money on the transfer market. In the world of college football, teams will take whatever they can get if that gives them a chance to win. This is especially the case for a team like Florida State. Hammond absolutely leaves a hole on defense for the Cavaliers and his loss is further felt by the loss of depth across the front. Devon Baxter is the next most notable name to miss this weekend, largely a backup on the season, but several other depth players are also missing, leaving the Virginia rush defense susceptible. The good news for FSU is that their rushing attack is one of their biggest strengths, and Ousmane Kromah and Tre Wisner are more than up to the task . This game will still probably have some uphill sledding for the Noles to overcome, but this does at least display the obvious path for an FSU win and earn its first ACC win of the season. away.headline: FSU Football's Micahi Danzy Says Virginia Win Felt Like ‘Old Florida State’
away.source: Florida State Seminoles On SI on MSN
away.blurb: Defensively, FSU held Virginia to 205 total yards, including just 37 rushing yards on 40 attempts. The Seminoles recorded 10 sacks, limited the Cavaliers to 3 of 15 on third down and stopped all four of their fourth-down attempts. After allowing an opening-quarter touchdown, Florida State kept Virginia scoreless the rest of the way. Florida State delivered a performance it can build on Saturday, defeating Virginia 38-7 at Doak Campbell Stadium behind explosive plays on offense and a well-received disruptive defense. For Danzy, Florida State’s performance against Virginia brought back a familiar feeling. The Seminoles scored 38 unanswered points while their defense recorded 10 sacks, giving both sides of the ball something to build on. 'It Felt Like Old Florida State' “It was amazing. You know, it felt like old Florida State being dominant on just both sides of the ball,” Danzy said after Monday's practice. Florida State finished with 464 yards of total offense, including 281 rushing yards and 183 passing yards. The Seminoles averaged 7.1 yards per play and scored touchdowns on all four red-zone trips. 'It Was Just Another Practice to Us' When asked about the team’s confidence following a strong week of practice, Danzy said the explosiveness carried into Saturday’s game. “So it just translated to the game like it was just another practice to us it felt like,” Danzy continued. “So that’s all it was to us. Just another practice.” Through five games this season, Danzy has caught 15 passes for 243 yards and added 28 rushing yards on three carries. In 21 career games at Florida State, he has totaled 43 receptions for 852 yards and three touchdowns, along with 249 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 17 carries. “So we just executed what we’ve been practicing,” Danzy said. “That’s all we did like what we’ve been practicing.” Florida State’s defense held Virginia to 205 total yards, including just 37 rushing yards on 40 attempts, while recording 10 sacks. The Cavaliers converted only three of 15 third-down attempts and went 0 for 4 on fourth down. “We had five three-and-outs,” head coach Mike Norvell said on Monday. “That’s a dominant style of defense.” The defense also recorded 12 tackles for loss, further showcasing a dominant performance. The Seminoles now have to carry that execution on the road when they face Louisville on Friday at 7 p.m. ET Friday on ESPN, with a chance to build on their first ACC win of the season. (Photo by Nathanial George/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images thehooch36 Mon, October 5, 2026 at 1:29 PM UTC Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads College Football can be odd. One minute, you're winning your conference opener on the road 31-13. The next minute, you're winning you're conference home opener 48-25. You don't look particularly great in either contest, but you cover the spread, hold up your end of the bargain, and sit 5-0 to start the year for the first time since 2016. That's the story of the Nebraska Cornhuskers. LINCOLN, NE - OCTOBER 3: Nebraska defensive back Jeremiah Charles (25) celebrates after blocking a punt in the first quarter of the game between the Maryland Terrapins and the Nebraska Cornhuskers on October 3, 2026, at Memorial Stadium in Lincoln, NE. (Photo by Nathanial George/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Nebraska took care of the Maryland Terrapins, albeit with one of the more dysfunctional beginnings to a game you'll see. A penalty on a (nearly) blocked punt that extended Maryland's drive, resulting in a field goal. Then after a three-and-out, an actual blocked punt that resulted in a Mekhi Nelson touchdown, his first of two in the game. Nebraska trained as much as 16-7, but still led 28-23 heading into halftime. The third quarter was a checkers match of moving a piece at a time, far away from your opponent. But the Huskers scored two seconds into the fourth quarter, and added two more touchdowns before the game ended. Meanwhile, the Nebraska defense held the Terps scoreless and relatively impotent after the 8:54 mark of the second quarter. Now it is time for the Huskers' biggest (and some may say first true) test of the season when the defending national champion Indiana Hoosiers make their way to Lincoln for Fox's Big Noon Kickoff. Curt Cignetti has his team in the top ten (top five in the Coaches' Poll), and even though there's no Fernando Mendoza, the Hoosiers are the only other team in the Bin ten to be undefeated. They have only been threatened once this year, when the Northwestern Wildcats of all teams gave them a scare, as the Hoosiers won that September 25 contest 29-23 at home. Indiana handled Rutgers this past weekend, and they mowed through their non-conference opponents (North Texas, Howard, and Western Kentucky) on easy mode. How will Nebraska perform against a rated team? Can they break the streak and knock off a ranked opponent? Would the rebuild fully be "on" if such a feat were to occur? Regardless of our collective thoughts on the outcome of the game, Vegas isn't counting on it. The line on FanDuel Sportsbook has Indiana as a 7.5-point favorite, marking the first time this season that Nebraska entered as the underdog. The over/under for the contest is 52.5 points. Bet your heart, but do so responsibly. Big Noon Kickoff between Nebraska and Indiana is Saturday at 11:00am Central, LIVE from Memorial Stadium, on Fox!

picks.headline: Early Indiana vs. Nebraska betting odds put Hoosiers on upset alert
picks.blurb: Early Indiana vs. Nebraska betting odds put Hoosiers on upset alert Skip to main content About Hoosiers News Indiana Basketball Indiana Football Indiana Baseball FanSided NCAA Sites Indiana Basketball Indiana Basketball Recruiting Indiana Football Indiana Football Recruiting Following a convincing 47-15 win over Rutgers on Saturday night, the Indiana Hoosiers are off to a 5-0 start and have extended their winning streak to 21 games. As we've seen before, Curt Cignetti tends to have his team playing better and better as the season goes on. Hoosier fans are hoping that trend continues, as the schedule gets a whole lot tougher from here. In Week 6, Indiana hits the road once again. This time the Hoosiers are heading west to take on the Nebraska Cornhuskers in a matchup between a pair of 5-0 teams. It starts a tough stretch of matchups for Indiana that also features battles against No. 5 Ohio State, at Michigan, vs Minnesota, and No. 19 USC. But first come the Cornhuskers. Early betting odds have been released for Saturday's matchup between the Hoosiers and Huskers, and it's clear that this is Indiana's toughest test so far this season. Oddsmakers expect a close game between the Hoosiers and Cornhuskers Indiana's first five games of the season have all seen the Hoosiers favored by at least three touchdowns. That changes in Week 6 against Nebraska. Via DraftKings Sportsbook, the Hoosiers are listed as 7.5-point favorites heading into Lincoln. Nebraska has been flying under-the-radar so far this season, but this gives Matt Rhule and company to make a serious statement. The total, or over/under, is listed at 51.5. Here is a closer look at the full Indiana vs Nebraska betting odds. Moneyline Indiana (-305) Nebraska (+245) Spread Indiana -7.5 (-105) Nebraska +7.5 (-115) Total Over 51.5 (-118) Under 51.5 (-102) Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Indiana can't afford to overlook Nebraska in any way The Ohio State Buckeyes come to Bloomington in Week 7 for what is one of the most anticipated games of the entire college football season. Thus, this matchup at Nebraska can be considered a classic look-ahead spot for Indiana. But the Hoosiers can't afford to let their guard down. Nebraska has been a middle to bottom-tier Big Ten program in recent years. The Scott Frost era was brutal, and the Matt Rhule era hasn't been able to pick up much steam yet. However, the Huskers are playing solid football right now and are coming off back-to-back wins over Michigan State and Maryland by a combined score of 79-36. Memorial Stadium in Lincoln is always rocking, and in a matchup between a pair of undefeated teams, it is sure to be raucous environment once again. Indiana has faced Nebraska once under Cignetti's leadership, and it resulted in a lopsided 56-7 Hoosier win back on Oct. 19, 2024. Nebraska had 5-star freshman Dylan Raiola at QB in that matchup, and he is now off to Oregon. Anthony Colandrea is now leading the Husker offense, and he brings a solid mix of talent and experience to the table. Now in his fourth year as a college football starting quarterback, Colandrea has completed 65.7% of his passes for 1,142 yards and 13 touchdowns with just two interceptions this season. He's also added 249 yards and a pair of scores on the ground. With a much more experienced starter at the helm, the IU defense has to be ready for whatever Colandrea and the Cornhuskers throw at them. On paper, the Hoosiers have a talent edge over the Cornhuskers. They also have the best coach in the country leading the way. That should give IU fans plenty of confidence heading into this Week 6 clash. But still, it's imperative that the Hoosiers don't overlook the Huskers in any way. Kick-off is set for Noon ET on FOX. Indiana Continues to Dominate Indiana improved to 5-0 with a 47-15 road victory over Rutgers, continuing one of the strongest starts in the country. The Hoosiers entered that game already averaging more than 40 points per contest and then produced another dominant offensive performance. The defense has been equally important. Indiana entered October allowing fewer than 10 points per game, giving the Hoosiers an enormous margin for error. They don’t need the offense to score on every possession because opponents have struggled to sustain drives. The challenge Saturday is the combination of Nebraska’s defense and the environment in Lincoln. Indiana has looked like the superior team, but laying close to double digits on the road against an unbeaten opponent requires the Hoosiers to continue playing at an exceptionally high level. Indiana can win without covering 9.5. Pick: Under 51.5 The Under 51.5 is the total pick. Both teams entered October ranked among the national leaders in scoring defense, and Nebraska has the ability to make Indiana work considerably harder for points than Rutgers did. The Cornhuskers should also prefer a controlled game that limits Indiana’s possessions. A score around 27-20 fits the matchup and stays comfortably below the total. Here’s a Nebraska vs Indiana prediction. We will look at this from a betting perspective and determine the best Nebraska vs Indiana pick. Indiana Hoosiers Betting Preview This year the Hoosiers got off to a pretty dominant start. Indiana opened with a blowout win over North Texas 52-16, then dispatched Howard 55-0 in game two. The Hoosiers kept it going with another blowout win, this time 38-0 over Western Kentucky. Game four was a lot closer but still a win for Indiana. That one finished 29-23 over Northwestern on September 25. In last weekend’s matchup versus Rutgers, the Hoosiers got right to work with 10 first-quarter points and hit the break with a 23-0 edge. Indiana kept it going from there and walked away with a nice road win 47-15. QB Josh Hoover put up a 20-of-27 line for 251 yards and four touchdowns. Turbo Richard led the rush with a whopping 204 yards and one TD on 13 totes. Nebraska Cornhuskers Betting Preview Over on the Cornhuskers’ side, they also started out hot this year with a nice string of wins. Nebraska rolled past Ohio 49-21 in the opener then took care of Bowling Green in blowout fashion 56-7. Game three versus North Dakota was also a win 34-7, then came another big victory on the road versus Michigan State. That one finished with a 31-13 score. Matched up against Maryland last weekend the Cornhuskers came out of a wild first quarter with a 16-7 deficit. Nebraska really got it going in the fourth quarter though, adding three more end-zone trips for a 48-23 victory in the end. Quarterback Anthony Colandrea was 26-of-39 for 238 yards, three TDs and one pick while also leading the rush on 10 carries for 108 yards. Indiana has recorded the equal-most home wins by a margin of 30+ points of any FBS team this season (3). Indiana has recorded the most home wins by a margin of 35+ points of any FBS team this season (3). Nebraska vs Indiana Prediction I’ll stick with the Hoosiers. Indiana didn’t have too many issues with Rutgers last weekend, bagging 593 yards, 26 first downs, 329 rush yards and 5-of-10 on third-down tries. The Hoosiers gave up just nine first downs on the other side with only 2-of-14 on third-down conversions. Indiana is cooking right now; four of their five wins have featured 38 or more points, and three of them have 47 or more points. As for Nebraska, they really got it going late in the game against Maryland, holding the Terrapins to just 1-of-14 on third downs. Offensively the Cornhuskers put up 447 yards and 209 rush yards. It was a messy game though, with Nebraska contributing 16 of the game’s 28 total flags for 132 yards. They’ll have their hands full with Indiana. away.headline: Indiana Availability Report: Lee Beebe's Status and Who's Out vs Rutgers
away.blurb: Indiana Availability Report: Lee Beebe's Status and Who's Out vs Rutgers Skip to main content SI.COM Indiana could be without its leading rusher Saturday night when the Hoosiers take on Rutgers, with running back Lee Beebe Jr. listed as a game-time decision, per the Big Ten's availability report . Beebe, who rushed for 203 yards in Indiana's win over Northwestern last week, was a midweek addition to the availability report. His status headlines an otherwise encouraging final injury update for the Hoosiers, who had three players removed from the report ahead of their first road test of the season. Richard was listed as probable Friday before being removed from Saturday's report, putting him in line to handle the bulk of Indiana's rushing workload should Beebe be unable to go. Cuono, a second-year depth running back with 11 carries for 45 yards this season, would likely serve as Richard's primary backup in that scenario. True freshman Jayreon Campbell, who has rushed six times for 43 yards in limited action, is also available. Khobie Martin, meanwhile, remains out for the fourth consecutive game as he continues recovering from a forearm injury he suffered in Indiana's season opener against North Texas. Martin is expected to return around the midway point of the season. Indiana enters Saturday with a rushing attack ranked among the nation's top 10, although Beebe's potential absence would leave the Hoosiers without one of their most productive offensive weapons. Linebacker Rolijah Hardy, who was listed as probable Friday after suffering an injury late in his eight-tackle performance against Northwestern, was also removed from Saturday's availability report and is expected to play. A.J. Harris, Daniel Ndukwe among those ruled out Defensive end Daniel Ndukwe is also out, marking his first absence of the season. Ndukwe ranks second on the team with 4.5 tackles for loss, including 1.5 against Northwestern last week. Indiana still has considerable depth at edge, with Stephen Daley, Kellan Wyatt, Tobi Osunsanmi, Chiddi Obiazor and Josh Burnham available to help absorb his absence. Elsewhere, cornerback Carson Williams and wide receiver Lebron Bond remain out for the third and fourth consecutive games, respectively. Indiana and Rutgers are scheduled to kick off at 8 p.m. ET. home.headline: Jamal Rule's 'doubtful' status gives Nebraska a major concern with Maryland looming
home.blurb: On Monday, Huskers head coach Matt Rhule announced he wouldn't give any more player injury updates unless he absolutely had to, thanks to the new Big Ten availability report rules. The first availability report of the week was due at 7 pm on Wednesday and it turns out that Rule is listed as doubtful. At the end of the second quarter, Rule came back out of the Huskers’ locker room and tried running up and down the sideline. However, those who saw him try things out said he was still noticeably limping. The decision to keep him out for the rest of the contest was easier when NU scored a touchdown with just a second to go in the half, making the score 24-10. Jamal Rule doubtful for Maryland as Nebraska football chases first 5-0 start since 2016 In the past, Rhule has given injury updates during his Monday press conference during game week. However, following the lead of several other Big Ten coaches, he’s decided to wait until he absolutely has to tell the world whether a player is available. Wednesday’s availability report isn't the final word on Jamal Rule’s ability to play Saturday, though with him listed as doubtful, it’s clear he’s still feeling the effects of the injury. One need only look at the gamesmanship LSU head coach Lane Kiffin showed with his own availability report a few weeks back. In the first report, Kiffin said quarterback Sam Leavitt was “doubtful,” then gradually improved the prognosis. Leavitt started and played the whole game (and lost) against Ole Miss that week. This article was originally published on huskercorner.com as Jamal Rule's 'doubtful' status gives Nebraska a major concern with Maryland looming . After waiting and holding their breath since last Saturday evening, Nebraska football fans finally have the answer as to whether freshman phenom running back Jamal Rule will play against Maryland. Rule started the game against Michigan State last weekend but managed just four carries before he left the game with an apparent injury. For a time, it looked like Rule might come back in the second half. The potential absence of Rule is a massive one for the Cornhuskers, as he’s become one of the most electric players on the Nebraska football team early in the season. Not only that but he’s been one of the most electric freshmen in the entire country. Rule’s 333 rushing yards lead all first-year players, and he’s scored 6 touchdowns (5 rushing and 1 receiving) in just three full games. The phenom is averaging an incredible 7.9 yards per carry. The new rules require Big Ten coaches to release four availability reports. The next two will be on Thursday and Friday night, followed by a final, decisive one on Saturday morning. It seems unlikely that Matt Rhule would engage in that kind of gamesmanship for Nebraska’s showdown with Maryland, but something could change with Jamal Rule as the week goes on. home.headline: Nebraska Upgrades Jamal Rule and Jacory Barney on Latest Availability Report; Mekhi Nelson Unchanged
home.blurb: Rule was labeled as doubtful in NU's initial availability report Wednesday. He remained there Thursday before moving up to questionable Friday. His return would bolster a running back room with an alarmingly low amount of career production. After being upgraded from questionable to probable, he appears set to return against the Terps. That would give the Huskers a key piece in both their passing and return games. If he sits this one out, more catches could be in store for Quinn Clark and Keelan Smith. Isaiah Mozee and Andrew Marshall are options as punt returners. The surprising news came Thursday when junior running back Mekhi Nelson was added to the availability report as questionable. That status stayed the same on Friday. Nelson's availability would provide a significant boost for the Huskers on the ground against Maryland. With Jamal Rule also questionable, NU could enter Saturday's contest without their two most productive backs. Isaiah Mozee, listed as a co-No. 1 on the depth chart with Rule and Nelson, has 31 carries for 149 yards this season, plus three receptions for 37 yards. Backups Kwinten Ives, Vincent Genatone and Conor Booth have combined for 10 carries for 49 yards and three receptions for 38 yards. It’s not just Game Week, it’s RichRod Game Week! Arizona’s first trip to West Virginia will see it face off against former head coach Rich Rodriguez , who is back with the Mountaineers for a second go-around. Rodriguez coached there from 2001-07 before going to Michigan for three years and then spending 2012-17 with the Wildcats. The current West Virginia team is on a 2-game skid, losing a 45-42 shootout at Iowa State last weekend after falling at home to Oklahoma State in its Big 12 opener. To better understand RichRod’s squad, we reached out to Dillon Clark of SB Nation sister site The Smoking Musket for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his impressive answers to our mediocre questions: AZ Desert Swarm: West Virginia went 3-0 in nonconference play, including an impressive win over Virginia, but then has lost both conference games. What have been the main contributing factors to the backslide? Dillon Clark: “There has been a significant increase in competition in Big 12 play compared to our nonconference schedule. The win against Virginia looked good at the time because they were ranked, but after their performance against Florida State last week I don’t think they are going to be anywhere near the top of the ACC again. Our defense hasn’t looked great all year but the wheels have come completely off in the last two games. We have given up over 1,200 yards of total offense in the last two games which equates to about 3/4 of a mile if you were wondering.” It’s to no one’s surprise in Wildcat Nation that a RichRod-coached team is running the ball well, but this production seems to be at another level. What’s been the key to the rushing success, and how do you think Arizona’s defense will try to neutralize this? “We spent a ton of money in the portal on a quarterback, running back and several offensive linemen. Michael Hawkins Jr. has exceeded expectations at the quarterback position for us averaging over 100 yards per game on the ground 6.2 yards per carry. Many of his best runs are coming off of pass plays that would have resulted in a sack or throw away for most other QBs so when you turn those negative plays into big positives it really shows up on the stat sheet. One of the biggest surprises to me has been his elusiveness in the red zone and the ability to make people miss. I knew he was fast, I didn’t realize how shifty he is. Cam Cook has also produced at a high level in the RB position. He is such a tough runner. His yards after contact and broken tackles are what really sets him apart. Even though he isn’t what I would call fast, he has consistently popped big runs. He gets stronger as the game goes on and the majority of his yardage has come in the second half of games.” Quarterback Michael Hawkins Jr. is tied for the FBS lead with 11 rushing touchdowns, but how is he as a passer? Would you trust him if he had to be one-dimensional in this way? “I think it’s fair to call Michael Hawkins Jr. a streaky passer. The last three games he has started out looking a bit shaky in the pass game with off target throws. In two of the three he eventually settled in and made plays with his arm. The completion percentage against Iowa State was a bit lower than you like, but he did have a couple drops and throw aways in there. I have confidence in him as a passer, my bigger question is can our receivers get open consistently in a situation where we have to throw the ball, and can we establish an intermediate passing game? It feels like our passing game at times this year has been all or nothing. The drive-extending, possession-style passing game has not been sharp. I don’t blame that on Michael Hawkins as much as I do on play calling and scheme. I have a hard time seeing anyone making him purely one dimensional as a passer this year. Teams may shut down our traditional running game, but we have seen teams put multiple spies on him in the past few weeks and he is still escaping the pocket for chunk yardage.” The Mountaineers’ defensive numbers are not good, ranking last in the Big 12 in almost every category. Is this a talent issue, a problem with the scheme, or both? “In order to be as bad as we have been, it has to be all of the above right? Our tackling is bad. Missed assignments on nearly every possession.We can’t get pressure on the quarterback. When we are in the right place we end up with a pass interference penalty. It’s rough all around. There has been a lot of talk on if Zac Alley’s reputation as a sort of ‘mad scientist’ on defense could be part of the problem. It’s really hard to argue against that when you see us consistently confused on pre-snap alignments. The biggest concern is that we are struggling in every aspect. Scoring defense, rushing defense, pass defense, total yardage, it doesn’t matter which stat you look at, we are at or near the bottom. The only hope is that potentially our two best defenders just became eligible last week. Jacorey Thomas and Jason Chambers should help plug some holes in what has been a leaky secondary. There is only one way for us to go from here.” How has the second coming of RichRod been so far in your estimation? Have there been any classic moments in terms of his antics? “After the Virginia win in Week 3 the vibes around the WVU fan base were as high as I’ve seen them in a very long time. That game brought back a lot of great memories from Rich Rod’s first tenure here and it felt like the sky was the limit. The last two weeks have put a damper on the mood though the fact that the offense has been producing at a high level still does take some of the blame off of him. The Rich Rod offense is back and it’s humming, but how did he not see this coming with the defense? There was definitely a group of the fanbase that didn’t want him back, and those voices are getting louder with each loss. I think he has shown enough so far that the majority of the fan base still believes he can get this right. We love that he holds players accountable in the moment, and it gives us hope that he can turn this thing around.” Prediction time. Does Arizona beat its former coach and get a big conference road win or do the Mountaineers hold serve at home? Give us a score prediction. “We have the worst defense in the Big 12. You have one of the best offenses. We are coming off of two straight brutal conference losses. You are coming off of a dominant win against a previously undefeated Cincinnati team. In other words, we have you right where we want you. 45-31 Mountaineers get back on track at home.” Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. Former Oklahoma, Houston and Tarleton State player Cody Jackson erupted for 160 receiving yards in the Cyclones’ momentum swing-filled 45-42 triumph over West Virginia at Jack Trice Stadium. Oct 3, 2026 Updated Oct 3, 2026 AMES — Cody Jackson transferred to Iowa State last winter in search of his fourth fresh start. The talented transfer wide receiver found it, but catches proved tough to come by. Until Saturday, when the former Oklahoma, Houston and Tarleton State player erupted for 160 receiving yards in the Cyclones’ momentum swing-filled 45-42 triumph over West Virginia at Jack Trice Stadium. “I trusted in God, number one, and trusted in my coaches (and) my teammates,” said Jackson, who didn’t record a catch in ISU’s first two games, but now has 12 receptions in the past two games. “Not having my head down. Keeping my head high. Keeping a smile on my face every day and coming in and working at practice.” Jackson’s first grab on Saturday for the Cyclones (3-2, 1-1 Big 12) turned into a 46-yard touchdown on a halfback toss from Aiden Flora. His other seven receptions against the Mountaineers (3-3, 0-2) came during a tense second half, and many fueled three straight scoring drives that helped ISU preserve the win. “He did a great job finding open windows and attacking the ball in the air,” Cyclones quarterback Jaylen Raynor said. Jackson notched 92 yards after the catch and often adjusted his routes as Raynor improvised amid amped up West Virginia pressure. His 43-yard catch on third-and-six early in the fourth quarter set up Kyle Konrardy’s 35-yard field goal that gave ISU a 31-28 lead. And Jackson’s 15-yard grab on the Cyclones’ final scoring drive ended in one of Flora’s three rushing touchdowns. Flora’s now averaging 8.1 yards per carry and has rushed for 600 yards and six touchdowns. “(He’s) a great leader,” Jackson said. “He can do everything, like you could see. away.headline: Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane
away.blurb: "It's very hard to play perfect,'' said Monken, who also points out the margin for error is slim for his West Point teams. "We're going to strive to it.'' Monken pointed out that Army had too many missed assignments, played with poor fundamentals at times and didn't help themselves with six penalties, but he's not given up on the squad. This article originally appeared on Times Herald-Record: Army football seeks bounce back in return to home action vs. Tulane In the end, Army's 21-19 loss at Louisiana Tech on Saturday night was just a non-conference game and didn't affect the American Conference standings. However, the Black Knights are having trouble building on positives. A dominant win over Bryant in the opener, followed by a crushing late loss at home to South Florida. A tough road win over Temple, followed by a stumbling loss as a small favorite at Louisiana Tech , dropping the Black Knights to 2-2. "We're not going to let this game kind of derail our season,'' said senior center and co-captain Brady Small. "We're going to go back, we're going to watch some film, we're going to learn and get ready for Tulane, another conference game. So just use this as fuel to the fire to get us a win at home.'' Army is a three-point favorite over Tulane for Saturday's noon ET start. Army is 1-1 in American action, and needs a win vs. the Green Wave to stay in contact with the 1-0 leaders: Florida Atlantic (4-1 overall), Memphis (4-1), Texas San Antonio (4-1), Alabama Birmingham (3-2) and North Texas (3-2). Army will face FAU and Memphis but not the other three this season. "Honestly, we've just got to attack the adversity at hand,'' said back Samari Howard. "We can't let this be a lull in our preparation. Overall, we've got to come together as a collective and tackle the adversity and get ready for the next week and the week after that.'' "I don't believe anybody loses momentum unless they stop believing,'' head coach Jeff Monken said. "And I don't think our guys will stop believing. ... If we allow it to derail us, then shame on us. Weve got to learn from it, and each game is independent of the last one. I don't think we allowed last week (win over Temple) to linger into this week. We weren't patting ourselves on the back for such a great job.'' Monken always reminds people that winning college football games is hard. "I love our team,'' he said. "They're tough as nails. They compete, and we played all the way to the end tonight.'' West Point and New Orleans are separated by more than 1,300 miles, but the football programs at Army and Tulane remain very familiar. The Green Wave have a long history with the Black Knights, dating back to 1953 when the two schools battled to a scoreless draw. Next to service academy rivals Navy and Air Force, Army and Tulane have met quite often, 21 times since 1996. Early Texas vs Oklahoma spread pick: Texas -9.5 Kalshi probability: 47% While 9.5 points is a lot to cover for Texas in a rivalry game, the Longhorns have won three of the last four Red River Rivalry games by double digits. Photo By - Reuters Connect. Texas defensive end Colin Simmons (1) celebrates with the Golden Hat following the Red River Rivalry. One of college football's best-known rivalries returns for its 122nd edition in Week 6, as Texas and Oklahoma meet at the Cotton Bowl in Dallas at 3:30 p.m. ET (ABC), with the Texas State Fair taking place right outside. The Texas vs. Oklahoma rivalry , better known as the Red River Rivalry, has been played every season since 1929, with these two storied programs often blocking each other from winning a conference championship or, in modern times, reaching the College Football Playoff. Texas is the favorite and has won Red River in three of the last four years, making it a popular pick among college football analysts . Texas vs Oklahoma rivalry history: Red River Rivalry 8 (1940-1947) Longest win streak 6 (1952-1957) Largest margin of victory 977-401-34 (.704) Program record 962-355-53 (.722) Claimed national titles (recognized) Conference championships Heisman winners Consensus All-Americans Weeks in the AP Poll Weeks at No. 1 Bowl games (record) NFL draft picks First-round picks This is one of college football's most competitive rivalries because both Texas and Oklahoma have had national success . It also adds to the lore that Texas has been the more successful team in the Red River Rivalry, while Oklahoma has had more national success over the last few decades. Like a river, the rivalry has ebbed and flowed for decades, with Hall of Fame coaches taking over, ending losing streaks, and winning national championships. Red River is one of the defining rivalries in all of sports. The rivalry began in 1900 with a 28-2 win for Texas , and the Longhorns wouldn't lose to Oklahoma until the eighth meeting in 1905, when the Sooners won 2-0. Texas dominated the rivalry initially, going 8-1-1 from 1900 to 1907 (they played multiple times in 1901 and 1903). Then, Oklahoma finally broke through, going 7-4 against Texas from 1908 until 1919 . The only interruption (beyond 1918 being canceled due to the Spanish flu) was when Oklahoma left the Southwest Conference for the Missouri Valley Intercollegiate Athletic Association (later renamed the Big Eight), which initially didn't allow members to play neutral-site regular-season games. The programs played just three times between 1918 and 1928, but resumed permanently in 1929, with Texas and OU playing every season since then. When it resumed, the Longhorns returned to dominance, winning 15 of 19 games from 1929 to 1947. Then, Bud Wilkinson changed football in Norman forever. The Hall of Fame coach was hired in 1947 and would go 9-1 in Red River from 1948 until 1957, taking home three national championships along the way, That's when Texas made its program-changing hire of Darrell Royal. Royal, who played at Oklahoma under Wilkinson, arrived in Austin in 1957 and went 12-1 against OU from 1958 to 1970 . In total, Wilkinson went 9-8 in Red River, and Royal went 12-7-1. They laid the groundwork for these programs to be blue bloods today, and without them, Red River wouldn't be a defining rivalry. Of course, coaches like Bob Stoops, Mack Brown, and Barry Switzer have played key roles for the last half-century, too. Recent Texas-Oklahoma results Oct. 11, 2025 Oct. 12, 2024 Texas (-16.5) 34-30 (Oklahoma) Oklahoma (+4.5) 55-48 (Oklahoma) Oklahoma (+7.5) Oct. 10, 2020 53-45 (Oklahoma) Oklahoma (-2.5) Oct. 12, 2019 34-27 (Oklahoma) Texas (+10.5) 48-45 (Texas) Oct. 14, 2017 29-24 (Oklahoma) 45-40 (Oklahoma) Oklahoma (+11.5) History of the Texas vs Oklahoma rivalry When did the Texas vs Oklahoma rivalry start? The first Red River Rivalry game , then known as the Red River Shootout (renamed in 2005), was played in 1900. Texas won the first game 28-2 at home in Austin. The game has been played 121 times and has been held in various locations before settling permanently at the Cotton Bowl during the week of the Texas State Fair in 1929. Before that, Red River had been played in Austin, Norman, Oklahoma City, Houston, and Dallas. Why is the Red River Rivalry played at the Cotton Bowl during the Texas State Fair? In 1929, after Red River resumed as an annual rivalry game, both programs signed a contract to play in Dallas during the Texas State Fair . Dallas sits about halfway between both Texas and Oklahoma's campuses, making it a natural fit for a neutral-site game between these two rivals. The initial contract was for 10 years, but it became a tradition to play the game during the Texas State Fair, and nearly 100 years later, the tradition continues. Why's it called the Red River Rivalry? The name "Red River" comes from the actual Red River , which runs through the Southern United States. Named after the reddish water from the red beds of Texas and Oklahoma in its watershed, the river rises from two branches in the Texas Panhandle and flows east. It forms the border between Texas and Oklahoma, making it a perfect fit for the states' college football rivalry. The rivalry was previously known as the Red River Shootout until 2005 (the 100th game), when its sponsor, SBC Communications, renamed it the Red River Rivalry. What is the Golden Hat? The winner of the Red River Rivalry receives the Golden Hat trophy , a ten-gallon hat made of gold. Created in 1941, it was initially known as the Bronze Hat because of its color, but it was reworked in the 1970s to make the trophy gold. It's not the only trophy the winner receives, though it is considered the best. The other two trophies the Red River winner receives are the Red River Rivalry trophy and the Governors' trophy. Best moments in the Texas vs Oklahoma rivalry A controversial tie in the downpour (1984) The second game ever in which Texas and Oklahoma were the top two ranked teams in the country ended in controversy. On a rainy day in Dallas, Oklahoma head coach Barry Switzer wore a "Beat Texas" hat as the Longhorns led 10-0 at halftime. However, the Sooners bounced back in the second half and were up 15-12 in the final seconds of Red River. With 10 seconds left and in field goal range, the Longhorns threw to the end zone, and QB Todd Dodge appeared to be intercepted by Keith Stanberry. But officials ruled it incomplete, and Texas' Jeff Ward hit a field goal to end the game in a 15-15 tie. Roy Williams putting on his Superman cape (2001) With just over two minutes left and No. 3 Oklahoma holding a 7-3 lead, No. 5 Texas had the ball on its own three-yard line. Longhorns QB Chris Simms dropped back to pass, but Oklahoma safety Roy Williams hurdled a blocker while blitzing and deflected the throw. Sooner linebacker Teddy Lehman's caught the deflected pass for an interception and returned it for a touchdown. The play is commonly known as "The Superman Play." Caleb Williams' comeback (2021) In Lincoln Riley's final Red River Rivalry game as Oklahoma's head coach, his No. 6 Sooners trailed No. 21 Texas 35-17 with just over six minutes to go in the second quarter. After his second turnover, Riley benched starting QB Spencer Rattler for freshman five-star recruit Caleb Williams. Williams would lead a field goal drive before half but was still down 38-20 early in the third quarter when the future Heisman Trophy winner came to life. The Sooners would score on six of their final seven drives to win 55-48. Having led 28-7 in the first quarter, it became the game Texas ever lost after leading by 21 points. However, even as Texas has held Oklahoma to just three field goals over the last two Red River Rivalries, the Longhorns haven't exactly put on offensive showcases . This year, the expectations for the offenses aren't all that different, and the oddsmakers have the 2026 Red River Rivalry as low-scoring as the last couple of seasons. But don't worry, they still have the Horns coming out on top. The star running back was off the report just before kickoff and was seen on the sidelines in full pads, with his helmet on, but never entered the game against the Volunteers. However, when it comes to Terry and Townsend, your guess is as good as mine. Smothers is nursing a reported lower-leg injury suffered in practice, Townsend is healing up from a knee injury he sustained before Week 2's kickoff, Terry is recovering from a toe injury ahead of Week 2's game, Coleman hasn't played since Week 3, and Filsaime has yet to take the field this season. For right now, Texas fans (and Oklahoma fans) will have to wait to see what Texas's injury list looks like on Wednesday evening, because until then, Sarkisian is remaining tight-lipped about the health of his team. Texas Injuries Could Shape Red River Matchup Against Oklahoma LonghornsRoundtable 446 Members • 1,680 Posts LonghornsRoundtable LonghornsRoundtable Featured stories Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Scott Wachter-Imagn Images Texas Injuries Could Shape Red River Matchup Against Oklahoma Timothy Hamm Partner Oct 4, 2026 6:14 PM Published Oct 4, 2026 6:14 PM Texas enters Oklahoma week healthier after its bye, but several key Longhorns remain worth watching ahead of Saturday’s Red River Rivalry in Dallas. More Videos Texas football enters Red River Rivalry week in a better injury position than it faced at Tennessee, but the Longhorns still have several important availability questions before Saturday’s showdown with Oklahoma at the Cotton Bowl. The biggest positive involves running back Hollywood Smothers, who missed the Tennessee game despite dressing in an emergency role. MORE: Ex Texas Star Wins NFL Rookie Honor Steve Sarkisian indicated after the 20-17 win that Smothers was close enough to play if absolutely necessary. The following bye week gave Texas additional time to get its leading rusher healthy. That could matter considerably against Oklahoma. Smothers leads Texas with 198 rushing yards on 41 carries and gives the Longhorns another physical option alongside Raleek Brown and Derrek Cooper. Texas managed without him at Tennessee, but getting Smothers back would make life considerably easier for quarterback Arch Manning. Wide receiver Cam Coleman also appears to be trending toward full availability after suffering a bruised tailbone against Tennessee. Coleman returned to that game, and Sarkisian described the injury as nothing serious. His presence opposite Ryan Wingo is important because Texas needs its vertical passing game intact against an Oklahoma defense likely to challenge Manning with pressure and disguised coverages. The bigger uncertainty may be on defense. Terry’s status could be particularly important. Oklahoma’s offense will test Texas between the tackles, and having another disruptive interior lineman would allow the Longhorns to keep their defensive front fresh while freeing star edge rusher Colin Simmons to attack the quarterback. Simmons dealt with wrist and elbow discomfort against Tennessee but returned to the game and is not currently expected to miss Oklahoma. MORE: Texas Longhorns Visit 5-Star WR Commit Amid Bye Week, Flip Buzz Texas is 4-0 and ranked No. 1 entering Saturday’s 2:30 p.m. CT matchup in Dallas. The Longhorns have won the past two Red River meetings by a combined 57-9, including a 23-6 victory last season. Still, rivalry games rarely follow the script.

home.blurb: “So for me to be out here, I’m grateful. I’m just excited to be playing football again. God willing, I’ll play the best game of my life so I’m excited for it.” Oklahoma DT David Stone Ready to go vs. Texas After Injury, Bye Week Skip to main content SI.COM NORMAN — A smile flashed across David Stone ’s face when the Oklahoma defensive tackle was asked after Monday’s practice how he felt. “I feel good, man,” Stone said. “ The bye week did justice for me, so I’m ready.” Exactly two weeks earlier, Stone was unsure whether he’d ever play football again, much less be ready to play in the Red River Shootout. A dislocated kneecap, which Stone suffered in practice Oct. 21, certainly isn’t a minor injury but the junior avoided major structural damage and was able to play five days later in the Sooners’ 41-13 loss to No. 2 Georgia. If Oklahoma is to pull off an upset over top-ranked Texas on Saturday in the Cotton Bowl , Stone figures to need to be a centerpiece of the defensive attack. The team that wins the rushing battle generally wins the OU-Texas game over the past quarter century. And while it would be a surprise if the Sooners put up big rushing numbers on offense — they’re averaging fewer than 100 yards per game on the ground and just 75.3 over the last three. The defense, though, has been strong against the run so far. They haven’t allowed more than 152 yards on the ground this season and haven’t allowed 200 rushing yards in any game since the 2024 Armed Forces Bowl. Stone performed well against the Bulldogs even though he was just a few days removed from the injury. He was happy for the bye week after that loss. “I very much needed it, honestly,” Stone said of the bye week between Georgia and Texas. “I’m grateful that I had the time off to try to get my feet back under myself, especially my leg.It’s just — it was bad. “I’m just grateful to play football again, honestly.” Now, the Del City product will face the Longhorns for the third time in his career. Stone certainly has an appreciation for the rivalry. “As an Oklahoman, this is a game that you see growing up pretty much everywhere,” Stone said. “The store you go to, you see the brands, the logos, of both schools across Texas and Oklahoma.” But Stone downplays the thought that this game is bigger than any other. “Of course, it’s something that you’l see growing up and has a lot of meaning to a person,” Stone said. “For me, it’s just another game, honestly, because it’s the next game, it’s the next opportunity, because literally two weeks ago I didn’t know if I was going to play this sport again. picks.headline: Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown
picks.blurb: Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff Get Fantasy Plus NFL Power Rankings Rays top sloppy Yankees Week 5 Waiver Wire Falcons run over Saints White Sox up 2-0 in ALDS Early preview of No. 23 UCLA Bruins ahead of Oregon Ducks showdown Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oregon Ducks are in the midst of a much-needed bye week, enjoying some time off after a strenuous and pressure-filled first month of the 2026 season. Through four games, we've seen the Ducks start at No. 2 in the AP poll, drop to No. 6 after an underwhelming win over Boise State before losing to Oklahoma State, dropping them all the way down to No. 21. They then took care of Portland State, 84-0, moving them up a spot before a pivotal road matchup in Los Angeles with USC . The Ducks never blinked, even when quarterback Dante Moore had to leave the game via ambulance with a head injury, as backup Dylan Raiola and some timely defensive plays powered Oregon over USC, 41-27. It was as impressive of a win as we've seen from the Ducks over the past two seasons, and one that they badly needed in order to keep their goals of winning a national championship alive. Now, Oregon gets to take a breath and relax with a Week 5 bye. But that's not all that the players and staff are doing, as they'll be getting a jumpstart on preparing for the upstart UCLA Bruins , who will come to town in Week 6. We'll follow suit, providing an early deep-dive preview of how the Bruins ' season has gone so far, a breakdown of the offense, defense, special teams and players to watch with game and betting details to boot. Let's start with UCLA's resume, as they head into the matchup with Oregon looking to continue their undefeated season. UCLA's Resume Through Five Weeks Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins wide receiver Aidan Mizell (1) dances in the end zone with wide receiver Landon Ellis (11) and wide receiver Semaj Morgan (4) after catching an 83-yard touchdown reception in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Week 1: W 45-24 @ Cal Week 2: W 28-10 vs. San Diego State Week 3: W 52-38 vs. Purdue Week 4: W 52-3 @ Maryland The Bruins got off to an impressive start in the newly-hired Bob Chesney era, taking down the Tosh Lupoi-led Golden Bears on the road after a dominant second half. Chesney, who commanded James Madison to the College Football Playoff a year ago, relied upon several of his former Dukes that followed him to Westwood in the season-opener. The start of the season was strong, and so was last game for UCLA. The Bruins went into Maryland and stomped all over the Terrapins, picking off four passes and racking up 475 total yards. The early, 10:30 PT start didn't hold them back, as they jumped out to a 20-3 lead at halftime and only added to the lead after the break. Sandwiched between those two spectacular outings were victories over San Diego State and Purdue, with the offense carrying them in the former and offense in the latter, showing how well-rounded the Bruins are in 2026. Offensive Breakdown Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins running back Jaivian Thomas (21) celebrates with offensive line Hall Schmidt (65) after scoring a touchdown in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images While last season was discombobulated at times for the Bruins offensively, new coordinator Dean Kennedy — coming over with Chesney from James Madison — has brought a revitalized, intelligent and, thus far, highly-successful offense to UCLA. Kennedy has a history of elevating previously subpar offensive units, as he developed quarterback Kyle Trask at Florida, turned Holy Cross into the Patriot League scoring leader and orchestrated the ninth-ranked scoring offense at James Madison in 2025. Now, he's doing the same thing at UCLA with a spread-based system that emphasizes physicality and explosiveness at the point of attack. Kennedy's units have consistently been among the best at creating explosive plays, both on the ground and through the air. While the Bruins won't go under center much at all, instead standing in the shotgun or pistol, they aren't afraid to run it right down the defense's throat. Through the air, the route combinations aren't necessarily complex, but they make it easy on the quarterback to read with a progression-based system. Defensive Breakdown Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins linebacker Trent Hendrick (25) celebrates after intercepting a pass in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Also brought over from James Madison, Colin Hitschler is the defensive coordinator for the Bruins with a goal of instilling an uncommon physicality that hasn't been seen in Westwood for some time. And thus far this fall, UCLA has, for the most part, lived up those goals. The Bruins mostly operate out of a 4-2-5 defensive alignment, following the trend of opting to put an extra defensive back on the field over a lumbering linebacker. But make no mistake, the linebackers have plenty of talent to handle the middle of the field themselves, with a pair of seniors coming in at first and second on the team in tackles through four games. Hitschler isn't afraid to send pressure, having loads of success against Maryland in forcing the quarterback to make decisions under duress that turned into four interceptions. Expect more of the same come Week 6, with Hitschler putting the onus on the offensive line to protect whoever trots out at quarterback for the Ducks. Special Teams Breakdown Sep 12, 2026; Pasadena, California, USA; UCLA kicker Mateen Bhaghani (15) kicks a field-goal during the second half against San Diego State at the Rose Bowl. Mandatory Credit: William Liang-Imagn Images The Bruins have modest special teams units, with average kickoff and punt return marks with the same for the coverage units — though the return aspect could change in a blink with a pair of return men with elite speed waiting back there. In the kicking game, kicker Mateen Bhaghani has been solid in converting 4-of-5 field goals and all 23 extra points. It's his third season as the starter at UCLA, and he's made 82.8% of his field goals with a long of 57 yards — a massive advantage at the college level. Punter Curtis Gerrand also has a big leg, averaging 45.7 yards per punt on 15 boots thus far. Players to Watch Sep 26, 2026; College Park, Maryland, USA; UCLA Bruins quarterback Nico Iamaleava (9) passes in the first half against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images There's an abundance of talent across the roster, yet these three players will have to be accounted for by the Ducks if they're to get their fourth win. QB Nico Iamaleava 2026 Season Stats: 62-for-99, 820 yards, 4 TDs, 2 INTs / / 35 rushes, 143 yards, 1 TD Analysis: Iamaleava hasn't quite needed to show off his world-class athleticism this year, with his backfield mate stealing much of the thunder in the first month of the season. That's not to say the former Tennessee starter can't scoot, as he's run for 1,077 yards and 11 touchdowns in four seasons while tossing 38 touchdowns and 14 interceptions. Not the most refined passer, Iamaleava — like many college quarterbacks — feasts on short and long throws, but hasn't quite developed the intermediate aspect of his game. Still very talented, Iamaleava is commanding mid-to-late round draft buzz, though he does have one more season of eligibility remaining. RB Wayne Knight 2026 Season Stats: 49 rushes, 445 yards, 9 TDs / / 8 catches, 88 yards Analysis: Yes, you read that right. Wayne has nine touchdowns four games into the year, with six coming in the first two games. Standing just 5-foot-7 and 193 pounds, Knight makes up for his lack of size with elite speed, vision and playmaking ability. At James Madison in 2025, Knight broke off runs of 73, 59, 58 and 49 yards with 57 and 49-yard gains on receptions. Always an ability to hit a home-run, the Ducks will have to be cognizant not to lose Knight behind the Bruins' offensive line. LB Sammy Omosigho 2026 Season Stats: 37 tackles, 3 sacks, 4 forced fumbles Analysis: Though the Bruins added 2025 Sun Belt Defensive Player of the Year Trent Hendricks to the roster recently, he's still getting acclimated so we'll spotlight Sammy Omosigho here. The 6-foot-2, 239-pound four-year Oklahoma transfer has gotten off to a fast start at UCLA, leading the team in tackles and recording three sacks from his linebacker spot. Hitschler sends the former Sooner quite often on pressures and he makes plays as evidenced by his four forced fumbles in four games. When former Dukes coach Bob Chesney made the move to Los Angeles in December, he brought 11 players and almost his entire coaching staff with him. Several of those players are now starting for the No. 22 Bruins (4-0, 2-0 Big Ten), who will be at Autzen Stadium Oct. 10 for a 12:30 p.m. conference game against No. 13 Oregon (3-1, 1-0). Chesney has his new team rolling. Like the Ducks , the Bruins are coming off a bye week . In their last game, they defeated Maryland 54-3 on Sept. 26 and held the Terrapins to 181 yards and one first-half field goal. Chesney's last game at James Madison came at Autzen Stadium on Dec. 20 when Oregon won 51-34 in a College Football Playoff first-round game. Eight starters for JMU in that game are now at UCLA. Here's an early look at the Bruins. Who is UCLA's QB? Nico Iamaleava is thriving in his second season as the Bruins' starter. The 6-5, 215-pound senior, who was the nation's No. 1 overall recruit in 2023, has thrown for 820 yards and four touchdowns, and has rushed for 143 and one TD. Last year he was one-man show at UCLA when he threw for 1,928 yards and 13 touchdowns with seven interceptions while also leading the Bruins in rushing yards (505), carries (112) and rushing touchdowns (4). Other UCLA offensive standouts Running back Wayne Knight is second in the Big Ten with 445 rushing yards and leads the conference with nine rushing touchdowns. The former James Madison star is averaging 9.1 yards per carry and 111.3 per game. The 5-7, 193-pound fifth year was a second-team All-American in 2025 after totaling 2,039 all-purpose yards. Michigan transfer Semaj Morgan is the Bruins' top receiver with 14 receptions for 174 yards and two touchdowns – all team highs. Defensive standouts for UCLA Senior linebacker Sammy Omosigho has been terrorizing opposing offenses this season. The transfer from Oklahoma leads the Bruins with 40 tackles (27 solo), 7.5 tackles for loss, three sacks and four forced fumbles. Safety Ta'Shawn James, a transfer from Iowa State, has 24 tackles and a conference-leading three interceptions, including a pick-six against Maryland. Former Oregon reserve Rodrick Pleasant is in his second season starting at cornerback for UCLA. He was all-Big Ten honorable mention in 2025. The last time the Ducks and Bruins met Oregon defeated UCLA 34-13 at the Rose Bowl on Sept. 28, 2024, in what was the Ducks' first conference game as a member of the Big Ten. They led 28-10 at halftime and the only touchdown of the game for the Bruins came on an interception return in the second quarter. Notes: Oregon has won five straight against UCLA dating back to the 2018 season. ... The Ducks are 16-3 against the Bruins since 2000 and have won 11 of the last 12 matchups. ... UCLA has only one win at Autzen Stadium since 1998. That came in the 2004 season. ... UCLA has opened the season with a 4-0 record for the first time since 2022 when it won its first five games. That was also the last time the Bruins had a five-game winning streak. away.blurb: While Dante Moore returned to practice on Monday, his status was limited as Dan Lanning described Moore as being in a helmet and shoulder pads. This article was originally published on autzenzoo.com as What Dante Moore's return to practice means for his status vs. UCLA . The biggest concern throughout the bye week for the Oregon Ducks has been the health of superstar quarterback Dante Moore . The last time everyone saw Moore, he was being loaded into an ambulance to be taken to the hospital after a disgusting hit by USC's Desman Stephens II. The good news was that additional testing showed no further injuries in addition to the concussion, but concussions are serious injuries that a player can't be rushed back from. Entering UCLA week, everyone wondered whether or not the Ducks would get their star quarterback back for this Top 25 clash. The news that Dante Moore returned to practice on Monday only added fuel to the speculation about his status for the game. Why Dante Moore's practice status means more for the Nebraska game than UCLA While Moore was back in pads, Dan Lanning emphasized that the injury report will tell you more about his status for this weekend. Given that Dan Lanning is pointing to the fact that it was great to just see Dante Moore back on the field, it seems that this isn't going to be the week where he returns. The Ducks are likely deep into the game plan for the UCLA game, and stating that Moore got a little bit of work in on Monday would point toward the team planning for Dylan Raiola to start. Lanning could certainly be trying to get UCLA to prepare for Raiola just to play Dante Moore, but with the way he's indicated that the team is focusing on his long-term health, it wouldn't make a ton of sense for the team to put him back in the lineup right away. Oregon has seen that Dylan Raiola can lead the team to a victory in a tough game, and with the two weeks to prepare around his strengths, the coaching staff can feel confident in his ability. Raiola comes with plenty of Big Ten experience, and he's not going to be overwhelmed by any moment given his career experience. Dante Moore returning to practice is great news, but Oregon isn't going to push him to come back before he's ready, given the fact that his future is far more important. Moore has a ton on the line with his NFL potential, but you have to factor in long-term health with the effects of concussions, and the team will never feel bad for playing things safely with a head injury. It remains unclear if Moore will play or sit out on Saturday, as Lanning deflected questions around the star quarterback's availability to the Big Ten's mandatory injury reports that will be released throughout the week. "Dante was out there at practice for us today," Lanning told reporters on Monday. "Similar to what we said before, we're going to continue to make sure we do what's best for Dante as we move forward. Obviously, we'll have an injury report that's released later on this week that will detail what that looks like, but it was great to see him back out there with his teammates." "Dylan's got to keep doing what he's been doing," Lanning said. "Preparing like he's going to be the guy that goes out there every single day. We need that from every single person on our team. home.blurb: Cal was without quarterback Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele for the entire second half after he left the game in the final minute of the second quarter when he hit his head hard on the turf. He reportedly was cleared to return but Cal opted not put him back in the game with a head injury. Cal safety Kingston Lopa left the game with an injury three minutes into the first quarter and did not return. Bears starting nickel back Cam Sidney was ejected from the game for targeting in the first quarter. Cal defensive back Daniel Harris was ejected for targeting in the fourth quarter. INDIVIDUAL STAT OF THE GAME II: Cal limited all-Mountain West running back Jai'Den "Jet" Thomas to 46 yards on 16 carries. This game was considered a tipping point for Cal’s season, and it tipped the wrong way. Cal’s second straight loss reduces Cal’s chances to finish the season with a winning record for the second straight season. Before the season began, a 4-1 Cal record after five games seemed possible and a 5-0 start was not out of the question. A 2-3 mark at this stage was not what Cal supporters had in mind. The Bears have little momentum heading into the heart of its ACC schedule, which starts next Saturday with a home game against Virginia Tech. The outside complaints from Cal fans will continue, and the Bears are on the verge of becoming irrelevant this season. Cal rallied from a 24-7 halftime deficit to take the lead, but ultimately the Bears lost to UNLV 39-31 on Saturday afternoon at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas. Jackson Brousseau was the Bears' quarterback in the second half. Cal played the game without injured running back Adam Mohammed, the team’s leading rusher with 336 yards. RECORDS: CAL (2-3, 1-1 ACC), UNLV (3-2, 1-0 Mountain West) UNLV quarterback Jackson Arnold. Although he passed for just 158 yards, he threw touchdown passes of 70, 36 and 10 yards and ran for a 55-yard touchdown. He also had a key 42-yard run and finished with 110 rushing yards. With Cal leading 25-24, UNLV quarterback Jackson Arnold ran 42 yards to the Cal 12-yard line, which led to Arnold's 10-yard touchdown pass for a 32-25 UNLV lead with 9:38 left. KEY PLAY 1: On a fourth-and-2 play from the UNLV 47-yard line, Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele completed a pass to Tyree Sams, but it was a half-yard short of a first down. It turned the ball over the UNLV with 12:20 left in the first quarter with the game scoreless. It gave Cal a 7-0 lead with 11:30 remaining in the first quarter. KEY PLAY 4 : Cal starting safety Cam Sidney was ejected for targeting with 11:25 left in the first quarter. Steam is coming out of their ears. They are irate because the Alabama dynasty is not dead and they actually have to write good things about the Crimson Tide. Alabama (5-0) has run roughshod over their competition. The Tide has averaged 49.6 point per game and no game has been below 45 points in scoring for Bama. The Bulldogs have had a simpler schedule but have had similar results. UGA has averaged 51.4 ppg but the last two games have been 41 and 38 points scored. In short, these two teams score a good deal of points. In the preseason, Georgia was a FanDuel +2.5 favorite over Alabama. But much has changed and the the script has flipped. FanDuel now has opening odds of Alabama being a 1.5 point favorite over the Bulldogs with an Over/Under of 55.5 . So far this season, the sportsbooks have pegged UGA with healthy point spreads as well as decent sized Over/Under in each game. However ,most of them have been too low. Much like Alabama, the Vegas bookies have been giving UGA some pretty low numbers. They covered the spread and went over the points total in each of their first four games. This past weekend was the first bucking of that trend as the Doggies did not cover and had their lowest points total of the young season. In preseason, many observers figured Oklahoma would be a tougher competition. But who knew John Mateer would be such dog poo and gift the Bulldogs so many points? It is a mystery why anyone thinks a post-Diego Pavia Vanderbilt would be anything worth worrying about. Arkansas is in a deep funk. All that said, Georgia really has not played anyone worth a hill o' beans. To date, UGA opponents are collectively 9-15. Their Strength of Schedule is 97th. Alabama foes are 15-9. The Tide SOS is 23rd. The Las Vegas guys have underestimated the Tide all season. The Bama Boys have been killing the Over/Unders and had only one misstep against the spread. Sep 5 vs East Carolina: -28.5/52.5, Won 48-10 (-38, 58), Won/Over Sep 12 at Kentucky: -9.5/47.5, Won 45-17 (-28, 62), Won/Over Sep 19, vs Florida State: -18.5 / 50.5, Won 50-36 (-14, 86), Lost / Over Sep 26 vs South Carolina: -12.5 / 53.5, Won 49-18 (-31, 67), Won / Over Oct 3, at Mississippi State: -5.5 / 63.5, Won 56-23 (-33, 59), Won / Over The Crimson Tide did not cover against Florida State but easily did so in the other four games. It was mentioned in this space last weak that perhaps the FSU game was a fluke. Upon further reflection, it might just be the rapid pace that Bama QB Keelon Russell is developing and improving. The Tide offense is stacking up some points. Georgia and Alabama are No. 1 and 3 respectively in scoring in FBS thus far this season. The Bulldogs are putting up 51.4 ppg but that number is skewed by the 70-burger they put up on woeful WKU (1-4) who yielded 49 to Nevada. This Bama-UGA game will be the game of the week under a lot of spotlights. It will be the secondAlabama night game following the South Carolina match-up. Early forecasts are calling for rain in Tuscaloosa on Saturday. But that is what they were saying about the MSU game as well. With an over/under of 55.5 and 1.5 point spread by FanDuel , the final score could look something like Bama 29-27 or so. Does that seem logical? Once again, I am going over on both of these lines. Both defenses for these teams are better than either has faced, but it just feels like both teams will go over 30 points with the Tide winning by 5 or so. What do you think? By Cory Nightingale Published: Oct 4, 2026 · 7:51 PM EDT ESPN's FPI is seeing what most will see this week in the leadup to the massive matchup in Tuscaloosa between No. 2 Georgia and No. 6 Alabama . Saturday night's Week 6 showdown is, naturally, in prime time, with a 7:30 p.m. ET kickoff on ABC, as the SEC superpowers hook up once more with both teams ranked in the top 10 and plenty on the line on the second Saturday of October. By all accounts, this should be a game that comes down to the bitter end in T-Town, and that's what the FPI believes, too. At least for now, Alabama is a very slight favorite at home, and ESPN's FPI follows with that theme by giving the Tide a 52.6% chance to prevail and stay unbeaten. But because Bama is getting just over a 50% chance to win, that means Georgia is getting an almost 50% chance to prevail, too. To be exact, the Dawgs are being given a 47.3% shot to storm into Tuscaloosa and stay unbeaten themselves. Fittingly, both teams have the exact same overall record (5-0) and SEC mark (3-0), so something really does have to give on Saturday night. Not only is this a matchup that features 2 of the best teams in college football in 2026, it's of course a historical SEC showdown that features 2 of the most traditional powers in the conference's history. These 2 behemoths have played for plenty in recent years, and while Alabama leads the all-time series, 45-27-4, Georgia has won plenty over Bama in recent seasons, including beating the Tide in last year's SEC Championship Game as well as outlasting Alabama in the 2021 national championship game. Of course, 4 years earlier, almost to the day, Bama took down Georgia in overtime to win that thriller of a national title game to end the 2017 season. So, it's gone both ways in the biggest of moments, and Saturday night will provide another big moment in a rivalry like none other in the SEC. home.headline: Alabama's mounting injuries on defense may have been a blessing in disguise as talented true freshman bursts onto the scene
home.source: A to Z Sports on MSN
home.blurb: Griffin is getting more time in the lineup with Justin Hill and Desmond Zulu both out for the considerable future . So the immediate question became who would fill the void for Alabama’s defense. Griffin helped answer it in a big way. What stood out most was where Griffin lined up. He played stack backer, whether that was at the Mike or the Stinger, and he also spent time along the edge at the Bandit and Wolf positions for the Crimson Tide defense. Griffin was the highest-rated signee in Alabama’s 2026 class, and he has looked every bit of that. To be out there dominating as a true freshman tells you everything you need to know. This guy is going to be a problem for years to come. With two key defenders sidelined, the Alabama Crimson Tide turned to its highest-rated 2026 signee against Mississippi State. What he did on Saturday should change how Kalen DeBoer’s defense looks heading into a showdown with Georgia. Alabama’s win over Mississippi State on Saturday will be remembered as an offensive explosion. On the other side of the ball, though, the Crimson Tide got a breakout performance from true freshman linebacker Xavier Griffin. If not for injuries, that game may never have happened. Xavier Griffin vs. Mississippi State stats Xavier Griffin played all over the Alabama defense That’s a lot to put on a true freshman’s plate, and he handled all of it. Griffin finished the day leading the Crimson Tide with nine tackles. On top of that, he added a tackle for loss and a sack and a half. He was all over the football field against Mississippi State. Griffin is drawing a familiar comparison Griffin looked a lot like Jihaad Campbell did on Saturday. Maybe it’s the No. 11 and the build, but the versatility he brings to Alabama’s defense is insane. Few players can move from the second level to the edge and look comfortable doing both. That versatility is exactly why the Tide can’t afford to keep him on the sideline. Losing Hill and Zulu hurts, and nobody wants to see players go down. But because it forced Griffin into a bigger role, and now that he has shown what he can do, there’s no going back. Alabama needs Xavier Griffin on the field against Georgia The stakes go up in a big way this weekend when the Georgia Bulldogs come calling. Alabama is going to have to play its best game of the year to this point. There can’t be slow starts . There can’t be lapses in coverage in the secondary. There can’t be bad play calls. Against a team like Georgia, every mistake gets magnified. That’s where Griffin comes in. He needs to be on the field as much as possible, whether that’s chasing down ball carriers from the stacked backer spot or getting after the quarterback off the edge. Alabama is going to need every bit of juice it has against Georgia, and Xavier Griffin brings a lot of it. This article was originally published on A to Z Sports. Daryus Dixson still listed as questionable on Thursday night availability report Dixson did not leave the Week 4 loss to the Badgers, but according to Campbell, who addressed Dixson’s health on Wednesday, he was “dinged up” just before halftime. home.blurb: Penn State added a key defensive player to its injury report this week before visiting Northwestern on Friday night at Ryan Field. "We’re really fortunate in that room," Campbell said Wednesday after practice. "Jahmir played his best game that I’ve seen [against Wisconsin]. Zion gives us so much flexibility.
